description: Big-number sums, regrouping, estimating and word problems

lessons.title: Line Up the Places
lessons.intro: Big numbers are added the same way as small ones. The secret is to line up ones under ones, tens under tens, and so on.
explanation: Write the numbers one below the other so the ones digits sit in one column.
Add each column, starting from the ones.
4,231 + 3,546 = 7,777. No column went past 9, so nothing was carried.
lessons.rule: Line up the places, then add from the ones column.
lessons.tip: A neat column is half the sum done.

steps.text: Add the ones, then the tens.
Add the hundreds, then the thousands.
Put the digits together.

lessons.title: Carrying Over
lessons.intro: When a column adds up to 10 or more, the extra ten moves to the next column. This is called carrying.
explanation: In 368 + 257 the ones are 8 + 7 = 15. Write 5 and carry 1.
The tens are 6 + 5 + 1 = 12. Write 2 and carry 1.
The hundreds are 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. So 368 + 257 = 625.
lessons.rule: A column total of 10 or more sends 1 to the next column.
lessons.tip: Write the small carried 1 above the next column so you do not forget it.

steps.text: Ones: 8 and 7 make 15. Write 5, carry 1.
Tens: 6 and 5 and the carried 1.
Hundreds: 3 and 2 and the carried 1.
Read the answer.

lessons.title: Numbers in Lakhs
lessons.intro: In India we group big numbers as lakhs, thousands and ones. 3,45,678 is 3 lakh 45 thousand 678.
explanation: The places go ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, lakhs.
Adding works the same way however long the number is.
lessons.rule: Longer numbers need more columns, not a new method.
lessons.tip: Use the commas to keep your columns straight.

lessons.title: Adding Three or More Numbers
lessons.intro: You can add many numbers in one go. Stack them all and add each column.
explanation: Look for digits that make 10 in a column. They are quick to add.
In the ones column of 46, 37 and 54, the 6 and the 4 make 10 first. 46 + 37 + 54 = 137.
lessons.rule: Stack all the numbers and add one column at a time.
lessons.tip: Tick each digit as you add it so none is missed.

lessons.title: Any Order Gives the Same Sum
lessons.intro: Addition does not mind the order. 25 + 48 is the same as 48 + 25.
explanation: So you may start with the number that is easier for you.
To check a long sum, add the numbers again from the bottom up.
lessons.rule: Changing the order of the numbers does not change the sum.
lessons.tip: Add upwards to check a sum you added downwards.

quiz.question: What is 2,415 + 3,272?
quiz.hint: Line up the places. No column goes past 9 here.

quiz.question: What is 476 + 358?
quiz.hint: The ones make 14. Write 4 and carry 1 to the tens.

quiz.question: What is 6,789 + 2,345?
quiz.hint: Every column carries here. Add the carried 1 each time.

quiz.question: What is 125 + 240 + 310 + 95?
quiz.hint: Stack all four numbers and add one column at a time.

quiz.question: The library had 12,450 books. It bought 3,875 more. How many books does it have now? Type your answer without commas.
quiz.hint: 'More' books were added, so add the two numbers.
quiz.story: Meera's school library got new books this term.

quiz.question: On Saturday 18,640 people watched the match. On Sunday 21,785 people watched. How many people watched in all? Type your answer without commas.
quiz.hint: 'In all' means add both days.
quiz.story: A cricket match was played over two days in Pune.

quiz.question: What is 2,34,500 + 1,65,750? Type your answer without commas.
quiz.hint: Line up the lakhs under the lakhs. Watch the carry from the thousands.

quiz.question: What is 58,967 + 36,485? Type your answer without commas.
quiz.hint: Go slowly. Four of the five columns carry.

lessons.title: Line Up and Take Away
lessons.intro: Subtraction also works column by column, starting from the ones.
explanation: Write the bigger number on top and line up the places.
Take the bottom digit from the top digit in each column.
lessons.rule: Bigger number on top, places lined up, start from the ones.
lessons.tip: If a top digit is smaller than the one below it, you will need to borrow. That comes next.

steps.text: Ones, then tens.
Hundreds, then thousands.
Put the digits together.

lessons.title: Borrowing
lessons.intro: When the top digit is too small, borrow 1 ten from the next column. That ten becomes 10 ones.
explanation: In 52 − 27 you cannot take 7 from 2.
Borrow 1 ten. The 5 tens become 4 tens and the 2 ones become 12 ones.
lessons.rule: Top digit too small? Borrow 1 from the next column and add 10.
lessons.tip: Cross out the digit you borrowed from and write the new one above it.

steps.text: You cannot take 7 from 2, so borrow 1 ten.
Subtract the ones.
Subtract the tens that are left.
Read the answer.

lessons.title: Borrowing Across Zeros
lessons.intro: Zeros have nothing to lend. Here is a neat way round them.
explanation: For 5,000 − 1,234, think of 5,000 as 4,999 and 1 more.
4,999 − 1,234 = 3,765. No borrowing is needed.
lessons.rule: To subtract from a number ending in zeros, subtract from one less, then add 1.
lessons.tip: 1,000 − 1 = 999. All those nines mean no borrowing.

lessons.title: Check by Adding
lessons.intro: Addition and subtraction undo each other. Use one to check the other.
explanation: If 903 − 478 = 425, then adding 478 back should give 903.
425 + 478 = 903. The answer is right.
If the check does not match, look at your borrowing again.
lessons.rule: Answer plus the number taken away gives the number you started with.
lessons.tip: A ten-second check can save a whole question in the exam.

lessons.title: Finding the Difference
lessons.intro: Difference means how much more one number is than another. To find it, subtract the smaller from the bigger.
explanation: The difference between 7,250 and 4,875 is 7,250 − 4,875 = 2,375.
'How many more', 'how many fewer' and 'how much is left' all ask you to subtract.
Always put the bigger number first.
lessons.rule: Difference = bigger number − smaller number.
lessons.tip: Read the question again to see which number is bigger.

quiz.question: What is 8,694 − 5,273?
quiz.hint: Line up the places. No borrowing is needed here.

quiz.question: What is 742 − 368?
quiz.hint: You cannot take 8 from 2. Borrow 1 ten first.

quiz.question: What is 6,003 − 2,748?
quiz.hint: Try 5,999 − 2,748 first, then add back what you left out.

quiz.question: What is 10,000 − 3,456?
quiz.hint: Subtract from 9,999 and then add 1.

quiz.question: The bicycle costs ₹8,500. Arjun has saved ₹5,725. How many more rupees does he need?
quiz.hint: 'How many more' asks for the difference.
quiz.story: Arjun is saving up for a new bicycle.

quiz.question: There were 1,240 passengers on the train. At Surat 385 got off and nobody got on. How many passengers were left?
quiz.hint: People got off, so subtract.
quiz.story: A train left Mumbai with every seat full.

quiz.question: What is 50,000 − 27,643? Type your answer without commas.
quiz.hint: Subtract from 49,999 and then add 1.

quiz.question: What is the difference between 3,02,105 and 1,98,476? Type your answer without commas.
quiz.hint: Bigger number on top. Borrow one column at a time.

lessons.title: Rounding to Estimate
lessons.intro: An estimate is a quick, close answer. Round each number first, then add or subtract.
explanation: Round 4,872 up to 5,000 and 3,129 down to 3,000.
5,000 + 3,000 = 8,000, so the real sum is close to 8,000.
The exact sum is 4,872 + 3,129 = 8,001. The estimate was very close.
lessons.rule: Round first, then calculate, to get a quick estimate.
lessons.tip: Use an estimate to spot an answer that is far too big or far too small.

steps.text: Round each number to the nearest thousand.
Add the rounded numbers.
Compare with the exact sum.

lessons.title: Adding 99, 999 and Friends
lessons.intro: Numbers just below 100 or 1,000 are easy. Add the round number, then take away the extra.
explanation: To add 999, add 1,000 and subtract 1.
lessons.rule: Add the round number, then subtract the extra you added.
lessons.tip: 999 is 1 less than 1,000. 98 is 2 less than 100.

lessons.title: Subtracting 99, 999 and Friends
lessons.intro: The same idea works for taking away. Subtract the round number, then give back the extra.
explanation: To subtract 999, subtract 1,000 and add 1.
You took away 1 too many, so you put 1 back.
lessons.rule: Subtract the round number, then add back the extra you took.
lessons.tip: Took too much? Give it back.

lessons.title: Making Friendly Pairs
lessons.intro: Some numbers fit together to make round totals. Pair them first.
explanation: The pair 37 and 63 makes 100, so add them first.
Look at the ones digits: 7 and 3 make 10.
lessons.rule: Pair numbers that make 10, 100 or 1,000 before adding the rest.
lessons.tip: Ones digits that make 10 are a clue: 1 and 9, 2 and 8, 3 and 7, 4 and 6, 5 and 5.

lessons.title: The Same Digits in Every Column
lessons.intro: Some exam sums look long but hide a pattern. Look down each column before you start.
explanation: In 1,234 + 2,341 + 3,412 + 4,123 every column holds the digits 1, 2, 3 and 4.
Each column adds up to 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10.
So the sum is 10 thousands, 10 hundreds, 10 tens and 10 ones. That is 10 × 1,111 = 11,110.
lessons.rule: If every column holds the same digits, find one column total and use it for all.
lessons.tip: A few seconds spent looking for a pattern can save a minute of adding.

steps.text: Every column holds 1, 2, 3 and 4. Add one column.
So there are 10 thousands, 10 hundreds, 10 tens and 10 ones.
Check by adding the long way.

quiz.question: Round 6,812 and 2,190 to the nearest thousand, then add. What is the estimate?
quiz.hint: 6,812 is nearer to 7,000. What is 2,190 nearer to?

quiz.question: What is 3,456 + 999?
quiz.hint: Add 1,000, then take away 1.

quiz.question: What is 7,300 − 998?
quiz.hint: Subtract 1,000, then give back 2.

quiz.question: What is 46 + 75 + 54 + 25?
quiz.hint: Find the pairs that make 100.

quiz.question: A shirt costs ₹1,899 and a pair of shoes costs ₹2,999. Round each price to the nearest thousand. About how many rupees is the total?
quiz.hint: Both prices are just below a round thousand.
quiz.story: Kabir is checking a shop bill in his head.

quiz.question: Her scores were 198, 199 and 203. What is her total score?
quiz.hint: Each score is close to 200. Start from three 200s and adjust.
quiz.story: Ananya did well in three rounds of a quiz.

quiz.question: What is 2,345 + 3,452 + 4,523 + 5,234? Type your answer without commas.
quiz.hint: Every column holds the digits 2, 3, 4 and 5. Add one column first.

quiz.question: What is 9,999 + 999 + 99 + 9? Type your answer without commas.
quiz.hint: Each number is 1 less than a round number. Add the round numbers, then take away 4.

lessons.title: Addition and Subtraction Undo Each Other
lessons.intro: If you know two parts of a sum, you can always find the third.
explanation: From 25 + 40 = 65 we also know 65 − 40 = 25 and 65 − 25 = 40.
These three facts belong to one family.
To find a missing number, use another fact from the same family.
lessons.rule: Whole − one part = the other part.
lessons.tip: Draw a bar split into two parts. The whole bar is the sum.

steps.text: Start with a sum you know.
Take one part away from the whole.
Or take away the other part.
steps.tip: One addition gives you two subtractions.

lessons.title: What Must Be Added?
lessons.intro: A question may ask: what must be added to 3,480 to get 5,000? Find the missing part by subtracting.
explanation: Think: 3,480 and how much more make 5,000?
Subtract to find out: 5,000 − 3,480 = 1,520.
lessons.rule: Missing part = total − the part you know.
lessons.tip: The words 'to get' and 'to make' point at the total.

lessons.title: What Must Be Subtracted?
lessons.intro: Sometimes a number is taken away and you must find out how much.
explanation: What must be subtracted from 9,200 to leave 6,750?
Take what is left from what you started with: 9,200 − 6,750 = 2,450.
lessons.rule: Amount taken away = start − what is left.
lessons.tip: Start, change, end. If you know two of them, you can find the third.

lessons.title: First the Sum, Then the Gap
lessons.intro: Some questions hide the starting number inside another sum. Find that first.
explanation: What should be subtracted from the sum of 2,460 and 785 to get 1,900?
Step 1: the sum is 2,460 + 785 = 3,245.
Step 2: 3,245 − 1,900 = 1,345. So 1,345 must be subtracted.
lessons.rule: Work out the part given in words first, then find the missing number.
lessons.tip: Write down the answer to step 1 before you start step 2.

steps.text: First find the sum of 2,460 and 785.
Now find what takes 3,245 down to 1,900.
Check your answer.

lessons.title: Missing Digits
lessons.intro: In some puzzles one digit is left blank. Work one column at a time, just like a normal sum.
explanation: Look at 4_7 + 285 = 732. In the ones column 7 + 5 = 12, so write 2 and carry 1.
In the tens column the blank, 8 and the carried 1 must end in 3. The blank is 4, because 4 + 8 + 1 = 13.
lessons.rule: Find a missing digit one column at a time, and remember the carry.
lessons.tip: Put your digit back in and do the whole sum to check.

quiz.question: What must be added to 2,350 to get 4,000?
quiz.hint: The total is 4,000. Subtract the part you know.

quiz.question: What must be subtracted from 7,000 to leave 4,625?
quiz.hint: Take what is left from what you started with.

quiz.question: A number plus 1,275 equals 3,000. What is the number?
quiz.hint: Undo the adding: subtract 1,275 from the total.

quiz.question: When 846 is subtracted from a number, the answer is 1,154. What is the number?
quiz.hint: Undo the subtracting: add 846 back.

quiz.question: The album has space for 1,500 stickers. Riya has stuck in 875. How many more stickers does she need to fill it?
quiz.hint: Total spaces take away the ones already filled.
quiz.story: Riya is filling a sticker album.

quiz.question: The tank held 12,000 litres. After some water was let out, 7,360 litres were left. How many litres were let out?
quiz.hint: Start take away what is left gives the amount let out.
quiz.story: A water tank in Jaipur is being emptied for cleaning.

quiz.question: What should be subtracted from the sum of 3,042 and 869 to get 2,165?
quiz.hint: Step 1: find the sum. Step 2: find how far it is above 2,165.

quiz.question: In the sum 3_8 + 275 = 643, which digit goes in the blank?
quiz.hint: Do the ones column first and note the carry. Then look at the tens.

lessons.title: More Than and Less Than
lessons.intro: Words tell you whether to add or subtract. Read them slowly.
explanation: There are 735 girls. This is 145 less than the number of boys.
The boys are the bigger group, so add: 735 + 145 = 880 boys.
'Less than' in a question does not always mean subtract. Ask which one is bigger.
lessons.rule: Decide which amount is bigger before you choose to add or subtract.
lessons.tip: Say it in your own words: the boys are 145 more than the girls.

steps.text: Girls: 735. They are 145 fewer than the boys. Who is the bigger group?
The boys are 145 more, so add.
Check: the girls should be 145 fewer.

lessons.title: Two-Step Stories
lessons.intro: Many exam problems need two steps. Find the hidden number first, then answer the question.
explanation: A shop had 2,500 pens. It sold 1,180 on Monday and 765 on Tuesday. How many are left?
lessons.rule: Find the hidden number first, then use it.
lessons.tip: Write a small label beside every number you work out.

lessons.title: Totals That Overlap
lessons.intro: Sometimes two totals share a part. Adding them counts that part twice.
explanation: Three bags hold 30 apples in all. Bags 1 and 2 hold 17. Bags 2 and 3 hold 21.
17 + 21 = 38 counts bag 2 twice. So bag 2 holds 38 − 30 = 8 apples.
Bags 1 and 3 together hold 30 − 8 = 22 apples.
lessons.rule: Add the two overlapping totals and subtract the full total to find the shared part.
lessons.tip: Draw the three bags and circle each pair.

steps.text: Add the two pair totals. Bag 2 is counted twice.
Take away the full total to find bag 2.
Take bag 2 from the full total to get bags 1 and 3.

lessons.title: Sums Inside Bigger Questions
lessons.intro: Some questions ask you to add two groups and then use both answers.
explanation: 330 ÷ 110 = 3, so the value is 3.
lessons.rule: Work out each bracket fully before you use its answer.
lessons.tip: Brackets are little sums of their own. Finish them first.

lessons.title: Does the Answer Make Sense?
lessons.intro: Before you move on, ask whether your answer is sensible.
explanation: If 1,240 passengers were on a train and some got off, the answer must be less than 1,240.
Estimate first: 1,240 − 385 is about 1,200 − 400 = 800.
The exact answer is 1,240 − 385 = 855, which is close to 800.
lessons.rule: A good answer is the right size and answers the question that was asked.
lessons.tip: Read the question one last time before you write your answer.

quiz.question: Ravi has 480 stamps. Priya has 135 more than Ravi. How many stamps does Priya have?
quiz.hint: Priya has more, so add.

quiz.question: A school has 912 students. 478 are girls. How many are boys?
quiz.hint: Take the girls away from the whole school.

quiz.question: There are 640 girls in a school. This is 85 less than the number of boys. How many boys are there?
quiz.hint: Which group is bigger? The bigger group needs you to add.

quiz.question: A shop had 3,000 notebooks. It sold 1,245 in June and 980 in July. How many are left?
quiz.hint: First find how many were sold in the two months together.

quiz.question: The three baskets hold 24 mangoes in all. The first and second hold 11 together. The second and third hold 18 together. How many mangoes are in the first and third baskets together?
quiz.hint: Add the two pair totals. The second basket is counted twice, so take away the full total to find it.
quiz.story: Three baskets of mangoes sit on a cart in Ratnagiri.

quiz.question: The college has 735 girls. This is 145 less than the number of boys. 435 boys and 375 girls study commerce. Everyone else studies science. How many students study science?
quiz.hint: Find the boys, then the whole college, then take away everyone in commerce.
quiz.story: A college in Delhi has two streams: commerce and science.

quiz.question: What is the value of (22 + 44 + 66 + 88) ÷ (11 + 22 + 33 + 44)?
quiz.hint: Add up each bracket first. Then divide the first total by the second.

quiz.question: What should be added to the difference of 5,000 and 2,875 to get 4,000?
quiz.hint: Step 1: find the difference. Step 2: find how far it is below 4,000.
